major.title: Block-level scopes on blocks 0 and 1 are neither printed nor rejected: the `parsed.scopes.is_empty()` checks are dead code and SECURITY.md step 8's 'no … scope' is unenforced
major.detail: SECURITY.md:35-37 requires block 1 to carry 'no fact, rule, policy, scope or context' and src/token.rs:214 states 'blocks 0 and 1 reject every scope'. The enforcement is src/authorize.rs:193 and :254 (`if !parsed.scopes.is_empty() … deny`). That field can never be non-empty on this path: `Block::print_source` (third_party/biscuit-auth-6.0.0/src/token/block.rs:49-73) joins facts, rules and checks only — it never emits a `trusting …;` statement for `block.scopes` — and `parse_source` (biscuit-parser-0.2.0 parser.rs:990-1065) only fills `SourceResult.scopes` from block-scope statements, which are therefore never present. Rule-level scopes (`check if … trusting …`) are printed by `print_rule_body` (symbol.rs:283-300) and are the only ones the evidence record's B4 exercised. Empirical, root-key holder forging a canonical block 1 with `BlockBuilder::scope(..)`: `Scope::Previous` -> ACCEPT(policy=0), `Scope::Authority` -> ACCEPT(policy=0), `Scope::PublicKey(k)` -> DENY(auth.operation_denied) (authority facts no longer visible to block 1's own checks, so `tenant(..)` fails); in every case `print_block_source(1).contains("trusting") == false`. No escalation was found: a block scope only changes which facts that block's own checks see, and the decision authorizer's policies keep their default authority+authorizer scope, so a scope can only make block 1 harder to satisfy. What is wrong is the documented invariant and the dead check that pretends to enforce it; the actual guarantee is 'blocks 0 and 1 may carry any block-level scope, which cannot widen'.

major.title: The 6.0 printer still emits non-injective constructs that the extended guard passes: strict `And`/`Or` print as `&&!`/`||!` and reparse as `&& !x`/`|| !x` (LazyAnd/LazyOr + Closure(Negate)), `TryOr` reparses with a closure it did not have, and `Term::Date >= 2^63` prints as a 1969 date the parser cannot read back — the evidence record's 'every construct … either faithful or rejected' is false
major.detail: src/authorize.rs:415-421 `op_ok` returns true for every `Op::Binary(_)` except Ffi, and :409 `term_ok` returns true for every `Term::Date(_)`. The vendored printer (third_party/biscuit-auth-6.0.0/src/datalog/expression.rs:558-559) prints `Binary::And` as `{} &&! {}` and `Binary::Or` as `{} ||! {}`; biscuit-parser 0.2.0 has no `&&!` token (parser.rs:394-399 only `||`/`&&`) and reads `true &&! true` as `true && !true`. Empirical, holder-appended block 2 (no root key): `check if true &&! true` -> guard passes, token ACCEPT(policy=0), while the reprinted source evaluates to false; `check if false ||! true` -> ACCEPT while the reprint is `false || !true` = false. `(1 / 0).try_or(7) === 7` reparses with `Closure([], [1, 0, Div, Parens])` as LHS (binary had no closure) — evaluation denies (operation_denied), fail-closed but not faithful. `Term::Date(u64::MAX)` prints `1969-12-31T23:59:59Z` (symbol.rs:192 `*d as i64`), `Term::Date(1<<63)` and `253402300800` print `<invalid date>`; the parser rejects all three (parse_date: `unix_timestamp().try_into::<u64>()`), yet the guard accepts the block (R3 -> ACCEPT). Nested, mixed-type and variable-bearing sets pass `term_ok` recursion but fail earlier at proto->block conversion ('sets cannot contain other sets', 'set elements must have the same type') — fail-closed at load. Impact on the trusted validators: none — `canonical_operation_check` / `exact_expiration_check` (src/authorize.rs:299-341) match the exact op slices `[Set, Var, Contains]` and `[Var, Date, LessThan]`, so any extra op or unparsable date denies (R5 block1 expiry[u64::MAX|1<<63|year10000|u64::MAX-999|0] -> DENY(auth.biscuit_invalid)); R3 also shows `LazyAnd`, bitwise, arithmetic, set algebra, prefix/suffix/regex, length/type, negate/parens, comparisons, i64::MIN/MAX and bytes are faithful. What is wrong is the completeness claim carried by the immutable record evidence/reviews/bfc2c0d/PRINT-PARSE-INJECTIVITY-6-0.md:6,60 and tests/authz.rs:1631-1633 ('every construct the 6.0 printer can emit is either proved to reparse faithfully … or rejected up front by the guard'), and SECURITY.md:113 ('the `Term`/`Op` matches in the guard are exhaustive') read as a proof of coverage: by the record's own finding-C standard (a holder block accepted although its reprint is not a faithful rendering = CONFIRMED gap), `And`, `Or`, `TryOr` and out-of-range `Date` are unremediated instances of that gap.

major.title: Nothing machine-checked binds `third_party/biscuit-auth-6.0.0/` to the published archive: the registry checksum that Cargo.lock enforced for 5.0.0 is replaced by a manual procedure in PATCH.md, and the tree already deviates from what PATCH.md asserts
major.detail: Cargo.toml:23-24 `[patch.crates-io] biscuit-auth = { path = … }` removes biscuit-auth from registry resolution, so Cargo.lock carries no checksum for it and deny.toml `[sources]` (unknown-registry/unknown-git = deny, deny.toml:31-32) does not govern path sources — `cargo deny check sources` is 'ok' by construction. The only provenance control is PATCH.md's 'Qualification requirements' step 1 (re-download, verify SHA, unpack, diff), executed by hand. .github/workflows/ci.yml has no step touching third_party/ (grep 'third_party|PATCH' -> none; the Dependency policy job runs cargo deny/audit on the lockfile only). Executed here: the archive SHA-256 equals PATCH.md and the crates.io index cksum, `patch -p2` of upstream #306 applies cleanly to the archive, and `diff -r` against the vendored tree reports no source difference — the copy is what it claims, today. But PATCH.md:45-47 states that `Cargo.toml.orig` is 'byte-identical to the archive', and the file is absent from the vendored tree (present in the archive, not excluded by .gitignore); the record's own step 1 would already fail on this tree ('the diff must be exactly the #306 hunks and this file'). For a deny-by-default authorization core whose signature verification, datalog evaluator and token parser now live as ~32 000 committed lines, any later edit under third_party/ is reviewed by eye only — the class of silent guard-rail the fleet doctrine names.

minor.title: Holder attenuations written in datalog 3.3 idioms are denied as a class, and SECURITY.md does not say so
minor.detail: biscuit-parser 0.2.0 desugars `a && b` / `a || b` into `LazyAnd`/`LazyOr` with a `Closure` right-hand side (parser.rs:479), and `.all`/`.any`/`.try_or`/`.get` likewise need closures or arrays; the guard rejects `Op::Closure`, arrays, maps and null (src/authorize.rs:412,418). SECURITY.md:'Issuance and attenuation' says further attenuation is available without the issuer key; the only shape that survives is the crate's own `attenuate()` output (or hand-built blocks restricted to strings, dates, variables, sets and the pre-3.3 operators). This is a deliberate fail-closed choice; the constraint on third-party attenuation is undocumented.

nonBlocking.detail: third_party/…/src/token/authorizer.rs:654,665,673 unwrap `convert_from(.., &self.symbols)`. Every fact, rule and check in `self.blocks`/`self.world` was translated into `self.symbols` by `load_and_translate_block` (builder/authorizer.rs:478-502, all `?`-propagating) before the Authorizer exists, so every index resolves; third-party blocks are translated from their own `block.symbols` (:457-461). nonBlocking.title: Attack 5 — double load: both views come from the same `build_inner` and the SECURITY.md order 5-10 is the code order
nonBlocking.detail: `Biscuit::authorizer()` = `Authorizer::from_token` = `AuthorizerBuilder::new().build(token)` (token/authorizer.rs:56-58); the decision authorizer is `AuthorizerBuilder::new().fact(..)*.code(policy).build(&token)`. Both call `build_inner(Some(token))` (builder/authorizer.rs:330-366), whose block loading depends only on the token (symbols, public keys, origins), not on authorizer facts or policies; no limit applies at build and the guard authorizer is never executed. Code order src/authorize.rs: 95 root id (step 4) -> 121-127 guard (5) -> 128 revocation (6) -> 129 authority_principal (7) -> 130 validate_initial_attenuation (8) -> 131-140 tenant + remaining <= 900 s (9) -> 142-171 ambient facts + policy + build (10) -> 172-178 authorize_with_limits (11). The only asymmetry is cosmetic: a `build` failure maps to auth.biscuit_invalid on the first load and auth.operation_denied on the second (:171), unreachable because the second cannot fail where the first succeeded.
